The story uses original comparisons to deepen Clara’s estrangement and expose institutional impersonality: a nurse positions the baby with the confidence of someone “attaching a vacuum-cleaner accessory,” while Ben appears like “an actor demonstrating the life she had chosen.” Later, happiness “opened in her without permission,” making her attachment feel involuntary and morally unsettling. These images develop character and theme rather than merely decorating the prose.
